> Living doc. What is actually in flight right now. Read after LESSONS.md.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > The `?favorited=` filter compares the wrong column
**What happened:** `findAll()` collects the ids of the articles a user favourited and then
filters `article.authorId IN (:ids)` — the article ids are being compared to author ids. Even
once the `favorites` relation is loaded, the result is wrong.

**Rule:** when a filter is "articles in this set", the column is `article.id`. Read the
`andWhere` literally; do not trust the variable name.

### [.claude/knowledge/schema.md] schema.md > Data model (TypeORM entities, `synchronize: true`) > `article` — `src/article/article.entity.ts`
| column | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | int PK | |
| slug | varchar | set once in `create()`; not unique-indexed |
| title | varchar | |
| description | varchar default '' | |
| body | varchar default '' | |
| created | timestamp default CURRENT_TIMESTAMP | spec calls it `createdAt` |
| updated | timestamp default CURRENT_TIMESTAMP | bumped by `@BeforeUpdate()` |
| tagList | **`simple-array`** | stored as ONE comma-joined string column, e.g. `java,spring` — not a join table, not JSON |
| favoriteCount | int default 0 | denormalised counter, incremented/decremented in `ArticleService.favorite()/unFavorite()` — the join table is the truth, this is a cache |
| authorId | FK → user | via `@ManyToOne author` |

Relations:
- `author: UserEntity` — `@ManyToOne`. Not eager; `findAll()` adds it with `leftJoinAndSelect('article.author', 'author')`, `findOne()` does not.
- `comments: Comment[]` — `@OneToMany`, **`{eager: true}`** — every article load also loads its comments.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > An invalid token must be a 401, not a 500 (#79)
**What happened:** an expired or tampered token made `jwt.verify()` throw inside
`AuthMiddleware.use()` (and inside the `@User()` decorator on public routes). Nothing caught it,
so the client got `500 Internal Server Error` and the mobile app treated it as an outage instead
of logging the user out.

**Rule:** wrap `jwt.verify` and translate its errors to `HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED`. A guard that
can crash is a guard that leaks framework errors.

### [.claude/knowledge/schema.md] schema.md > Data model (TypeORM entities, `synchronize: true`) > `comment` — `src/article/comment.entity.ts`
| column | type |
|---|---|
| id | int PK |
| body | varchar |
| articleId | FK → article |

**There is no author column and no relation to `user`.** The RealWorld spec's comment object
has `author`; this entity cannot produce it. `addComment()` sets only `body`.

### [.claude/knowledge/schema.md] schema.md > Data model (TypeORM entities, `synchronize: true`) > Response shapes vs storage (what the frontends expect vs what exists)
| Spec field | Source today |
|---|---|
| `article.favorited` | **not produced** — nothing computes "does the current user favourite this" |
| `article.favoritesCount` | entity column is `favoriteCount` (singular) and is returned under that name |
| `article.createdAt` / `updatedAt` | columns are `created` / `updated` |
| `comment.author` | no data to produce it |
| `profile.following` | computed in `ProfileService.findProfile()` from `follows` |

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Authentication is not authorization (#6, #44)
**What happened:** any logged-in user could `PUT` or `DELETE` any other user's article. The
route is in `AuthMiddleware`'s list, so people assumed it was "protected" — but the middleware
only proves the caller is *a* user, and `ArticleService.update()/delete()` never compare
`req.user.id` with `article.author.id`. The Swagger `403 Forbidden` annotations on those handlers
describe a check that does not exist.

**Rule:** for every mutating route, name the line that compares the caller with the record's
owner. If you cannot, there is no ownership check, whatever the decorators say.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Never `Object.assign` a request body onto a persisted entity (#112)
**What happened:** `UserService.update()` and `ArticleService.update()` both merge the raw body
into the loaded entity. Any extra field the client sends — `id`, `password`, `authorId`,
`favoriteCount` — is persisted. The DTO type is a TypeScript annotation; it strips nothing at
runtime, and `PUT /user` / `PUT /articles/:slug` have no validation pipe.

**Rule:** copy the allowed fields by name, or whitelist with a validation pipe
(`whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true`). The DTO class is not a filter.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > Comments load eagerly, favourites do not
`ArticleEntity.comments` is `{eager: true}`; `UserEntity.favorites` is a plain `@ManyToMany`
with no eager flag. See `schema.md` for what that means for service code.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Authorization (ownership) — where it is enforced
**Nowhere.** The middleware answers "is this a valid user"; no service or controller method
compares the caller with the record's owner:

| Action | Ownership check |
|---|---|
| `PUT /articles/:slug` | none — `ArticleService.update(slug, body)` does `Object.assign(article, body)` and saves |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug` | none — `delete({slug})` |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` | none — and comments have no author to compare against anyway |
| `DELETE /users/:slug` | none, and unguarded |
| `PUT /user` | implicitly the caller (`@User('id')`), fine |

The Swagger `@ApiResponse({ status: 403 })` lines on the article controller describe an
intended behaviour, not an implemented one — nothing returns 403.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > The response envelope and the `RO` suffix
`RO` means **Response Object**. Every controller method returns the RealWorld envelope, named
`<Thing>RO` in `*.interface.ts`:

| Endpoint family | Returns | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| single article | `ArticleRO` | `{ article: {...} }` |
| list | `ArticlesRO` | `{ articles: [...], articlesCount: n }` |
| comments | `CommentsRO` | `{ comments: [...] }` |
| user | `UserRO` | `{ user: {..., token} }` |
| profile | `ProfileRO` | `{ profile: {..., following} }` |

The frontends read `response.article.slug`, `response.user.token`, etc. A method that returns a
bare entity instead of the envelope breaks every RealWorld client (see `LESSONS.md`).

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Which routes are guarded (from the three `configure()` blocks)
| Module | Guarded routes (401 without token) |
|---|---|
| `UserModule` | `GET /user`, `PUT /user` |
| `ArticleModule` | `GET /articles/feed` · `POST /articles` · `PUT /articles/:slug` · `DELETE /articles/:slug` · `POST /articles/:slug/comments` · `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` · `POST /articles/:slug/favorite` · `DELETE /articles/:slug/favorite` |
| `ProfileModule` | `profiles/:username/follow` for **all** methods (POST follow, DELETE unfollow) |

Everything else is **public**: `GET /articles`, `GET /articles/:slug`,
`GET /articles/:slug/comments`, `GET /profiles/:username`, `GET /tags`, `POST /users`,
`POST /users/login`, and — notably — **`DELETE /users/:slug`**, which deletes the user whose
*email* equals the `:slug` param (`UserService.delete(email)`), with no token required and no
check of who is asking.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > What it is
A backend implementing the [RealWorld](https://github.com/gothinkster/realworld) API spec
(Medium clone: users, profiles, articles, comments, tags, favourites, follows). Any RealWorld
frontend (React, Vue, Angular…) is expected to work against it unchanged — **spec conformance
is the contract**, not just "it works with our own client".

Pinned at upstream commit `c1c2cc4` of `lujakob/nestjs-realworld-example-app` (2021-01-18).

**Refined prompt:** Trace where `comment.author` is lost between request and response in this NestJS RealWorld API, answering as a senior engineer on the codebase, with every code claim cited file:line. · Assumptions: "the app" means any RealWorld frontend reading `comment.author.username`; you want the loss point identified, not fixed yet.

You don't lose it — it is never captured. The author is dropped at the very first step: `createComment` never reads the authenticated user, so there is nothing to persist, no column to persist it in, and no field to serialize.

**The four places it is missing, in order:**

**1. The controller never asks for the user.** `src/article/article.controller.ts:77`:
```ts
async createComment(@Param('slug') slug, @Body('comment') commentData: CreateCommentDto) {
```
Every other authenticated handler in this file takes `@User('id')`. This one takes only the slug and body. The route *is* authenticated — `src/article/article.module.ts:28` puts `articles/:slug/comments` POST behind `AuthMiddleware` — so `req.user` exists and is simply not read.

**2. The DTO carries only a body.** `src/article/dto/create-comment.ts:1-3`:
```ts
export class CreateCommentDto {
  readonly body: string;
}
```

**3. The service sets one field.** `src/article/article.service.ts:101-105`:
```ts
async addComment(slug: string, commentData): Promise<ArticleRO> {
  let article = await this.articleRepository.findOne({slug});

  const comment = new Comment();
  comment.body = commentData.body;
```
`addComment` takes `(slug, commentData)` — no user parameter, so even a fixed controller has nowhere to pass it.

**4. The entity has no column to hold it.** `src/article/comment.entity.ts:5-15` has `id`, `body`, and `@ManyToOne(... => ArticleEntity)`. There is no `author` column and no relation to `UserEntity`. This is the hard blocker — the other three are one-line changes, this one is a schema change.

And the response type agrees: `src/article/article.interface.ts:3-5` declares `interface Comment { body: string }`, so `CommentsRO` (`article.interface.ts:20-22`, returned by `findComments` at `article.service.ts:165-167`) is typed to expose body only.

**What this means for the fix:** it is not a serialization bug you can patch at the response boundary — the data was never written. You need a migration-shaped change: add `@ManyToOne author` to `Comment`, thread `@User('id')` through controller → service, then produce `comment.author` as a profile object in `findComments`. Note `ArticleEntity.comments` is `{eager: true}` (`src/article/article.entity.ts:40`), so the new relation will load on every article fetch unless you scope it — worth deciding deliberately.

This is already tracked: `CURRENT_FOCUS.md` flags the same missing `comment.author` relation as the prerequisite for the 403 ownership check on `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` — the delete handler (`article.controller.ts:85-88`) has no author to compare against either, which is why its `@ApiResponse({ status: 403 })` at line 83 describes behaviour that does not exist. Fixing the author relation unblocks both.

**What I did not read:** `user.entity.ts`, `user.interface.ts` (`UserData` shape for the author object), the `@User()` decorator implementation, `profile.service.ts` (`findProfile` builds the analogous author-with-`following` shape you'd likely reuse), and any tests.
